evidence: Draft: "Have you got any sense of what it is that's making it feel fake?" for the SOURCE question "Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake?". It does what the_change says (Emulate's sample-co question, nothing else touched), and CONTEXT.txt holds it once, as the opening sentence of the 'It feels fake' section, directly before Joel's unchanged answer-shaped fragment "The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc." Meaning: the published guide says "First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you're trying to perform." The draft still asks the reader to find what about the practice feels fake, and the unchanged list that follows still supplies the same four candidates. 'what feels fake' became 'what's making it feel fake', a causal frame, but it adds no claim: 'what you are expecting' and 'a role you feel you have to play' are things that make a practice feel fake rather than things that feel fake themselves, and the paragraph's next sentences already reason causally ('it isn't necessarily about not having a grown up', 'a part that is protecting you'). Seam and voice: the section already has a British casual register ('see how you get on', single-quoted 'grown up', bare 'etc'), so 'Have you got any sense' sits with it, and the 'what it is that' cleft is the SOURCE's own. The second 'it' (making it feel fake) is the practice, anchored by the heading 'It feels fake' and by 'this' in the next sentence, so C02 is fine. Read as a spoken question it has no hedge, summary or tidy turn he would not write. Tell rows: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the literal draft in its context and found none PRESENT. Closest calls, all judged absent: T15 (it rewords the SOURCE question and keeps its shape) is not a thesaurus swap, since there is no rare word, the clause really changes shape ('feels' to 'making it feel') and the result is an ordinary spoken question; T19/T24 (a question followed at once by an answer-shaped list) is absent because the question is a real prompt to look inward and the question-then-list shape is already in his published guide line, not made by the draft; T26 ('fake' recurs from the heading and later 'the fake feeling') is the same as in the SOURCE, nothing new. Every other row (T01-T14, T16-T18, T20-T23, T25, T27-T29, C01, C03, C04) is absent: one 14-word question with no first person, scene, closer, reassurance, permission formula or contrast. Linter: 'D9 follows the source order' is one sentence replacing one sentence, so there is no order to follow and the rest of the paragraph is unchanged Joel text that does notice things (T13 and T09 not at issue); accepted. 'E36/E41 heavy second person' (7.1 per 100) is one 'you' in a 14-word question; the sentence it replaces also had one, and the paragraph runs about 8 'you' per 100 words on his own sentences, so the draft adds no second-person weight; accepted.
